To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students who have a profile of thinking styles that is more flexible (in relation to the three factors of the model of Sternberg & Zhang), show a better adjustment to the demands of the EHEA, and therefore, a greater probability of success.

the five profiles of thinking style obtained are: (1) The "Pragmatists", who are characterized by a pragmatic thinking style and a high level of creativity; (2) "The Analyzers", who are characterized for their analytical thinking style; (3) "The Balanced", who are characterized with a balanced thinking style and high level of creativity and (4) "The Theorists" and "The Pragmatic Theorists", who are similar in their high theoretical thinking styles
the students with the most flexible thinking style are those who have the best chances to adjust to the new demands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of thinking styles in university students, and its implications for the EHEA.
the analysis of the profiles of thinking styles and their implications for the adjustment to the new learning demands of the EHEA.
the study of students' thinking styles, and its relation to the adjustment to the European Higher Education Space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the profiles of thinking styles are a good predictor of the type of learning and, therefore, of adjustment to the EHEA.

the adjustment to the EHEA would be more difficult for those students who show a profile of thinking styles with high levels of both the components of the componential model of Sternberg: Analytical and Practical Thinking.

the EHEA is a challenge for all students but, in the same time, it is a challenge for the university itself, which should be able to adapt its teaching and learning to the demands of the new space of the European Higher Educational Area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results obtained are consistent with the theoretical model of Sternberg, but also, they show a certain variability in the students' responses that could be explained by the different academic degrees and their different levels of specialization.
the students who have a profile of thinking styles more adjusted to the new demands, will have a greater chance to adjust better to the EHEA.
, in order to improve students adjustment to the EHEA demands, it is important to consider their profiles of thinking styles and to adapt learning processes to each of them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students' thinking styles profiles have a great impact on the adjustment to the EHEA, and that this adjustment may be improved through an intervention on thinking styles.
the students who have more adjustment to the EHEA are those with a profile of thinking styles that is more creative, practical and flexible.
the adjustment of the university students to the EHEA demands will be more successful when the students have the appropriate styles of thinking.
